queue_order: Pilot (lane.memfast, 2 requests): GTA A1 then GTA B1 on the Thor. After the pilot verdict in pilots/lane.memfast.ok: GTA B2 A2 (Thor); Nightfire B1 A1 B2 A2 (Nova); Crimson B1 A1 (Thor); AUF A1 (Nova). Each: env HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1 docs/testing/request.sh --who lane.memfast --issue 507 --title <title> --route <route> --seconds 300 --perflog --device <device> --ref <a_ref|b_ref> --expect docs/testing/predictions/memfast-drop-soak.json. One handheld per title. On battery (owner 09-28).
window: title_verdict.py's own scored window (from the route's `mark gameplay`); [mf0] lines over the whole run, split at act=1
judge: python3 docs/testing/title_verdict.py on a COPY of each result dir (it writes verdict.json) for j_per_frame, gfps and reach; docs/lanes/memfast/mf0_read.py <result dir> for the census legs; logcat hakuX-crash for crashes.
prediction: #507 phase 1. b_ref deletes the XBOX load fast path: the five-instruction per-TB preamble (load xbox_ram_fp.active and cb_count, cache host_base in X26) and the per-load CBZ X26 + RAM/VRAM-window test ahead of the softmmu compare, and returns X26/X27 to the allocator. lane.vcpuplan measured the preamble plus test at 8.5% of GTA's vCPU thread with the armed leg never taken (PR #589 section 1.3), so B does the same guest work in fewer host instructions. a_ref differs from master only by the [mf0] census (instrumentation), which b_ref keeps.

legs.V (validity): Per run: the route logs `mark gameplay`; title_verdict.py reports power.measured true (on battery); >= 20 [mf0] lines. A run whose thermal record shows cpu3-7 paused inside the scored window is VOID for fps and J/frame (#507), not a zero, and is re-queued once. A run failing V is reported and re-queued once.
legs.J (J/frame, the point): GTA and Nightfire: mean over pairs of j_per_frame B/A <= 0.98 (plan: -3.5 to -7%; lane.vcpuplan's noise figure 3.6% per single pair, so two pairs per title). Refuted if B/A >= 1.00 on both titles.
legs.F (fps): GTA and Nightfire: gfps B/A >= 1.02 where A runs below 95% of target_fps (GTA 30, Nightfire 60); where A is at its cap the fps leg is VOID and J carries the claim.
legs.G (gameplay reach, exactness): B reaches `mark gameplay` on GTA, Nightfire and Crimson, with no hakuX-crash line and no hang (hakuX-perf lines continue to the end of the run) in any B run.
legs.M (census, A runs; decides nothing about: Per title from a_ref's [mf0] lines: the share of wall time after act=1 with cb=0 (armed); li/ln/lo and vi/vn/vo install counts; lnd/vnd distinct non-identity pages; the `[mf0] first` samples. Prediction, a guess labelled as one: armed share ~0 on GTA (vcpuplan saw the armed leg 0 times), and ln > 0 on every title (the XBE is mapped at VA 0x10000 onto kernel-allocated pages).
legs.S (vCPU share): Separate: a jitmix.py profile of b_ref on GTA shows the preamble and xboxchk roles at ~0 (A side: lane.ibcache's R1 capture on master, #507 comment 5878355210). Needs a held simpleperf window from lane.local (board request).
legs.pixels: docs/testing/predictions/memfast-drop-pixels.json: all 100 golden suites bit-identical per capture (queued by the arms job).
